title: Time-varying effects of left atrial appendage closure versus oral anticoagulation by reconstructed individual patient data from the randomised device trials

pico.population: Adults with non-valvular atrial fibrillation eligible for oral anticoagulation, in randomised trials of percutaneous left atrial appendage closure
pico.outcomes: Stroke or systemic embolism (ischaemic and haemorrhagic separately), non-procedural major bleeding, all-cause death, with landmark analysis before and after 30 days and 1 year
pico.timing: Procedure to maximum follow-up, with time-varying hazard ratios

decision: Whether to offer left atrial appendage closure instead of long-term anticoagulation to patients who can take anticoagulants, and in whom the early procedural hazard is traded against later bleeding reduction.
decision_maker: Electrophysiologists, interventional cardiologists and heart teams; guideline committees
why_now: Recent randomised trials in the appraised subset report non-inferiority for efficacy in anticoagulation-eligible patients (PMID 41910347) and in post-ablation patients (PMID 39555822), while a trial in high-risk patients did not show non-inferiority to medical care (PMID 41849741). Three pooled analyses of randomised trials appeared in October 2026 in non-target journals (PMIDs 42860016, 42862780, 42898218) using aggregate risk ratios, with an ischaemic stroke signal in one (RR 1.41 [1.07-1.85], PMID 42860016) that aggregate data cannot place in time.

competing.note: Randomised comparison of closure with novel oral anticoagulation, title as registered. Registry status RECRUITING.
Amulet versus NOAC. Registry status ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING.
Closure versus oral anticoagulation in a registered subpopulation. Registry status RECRUITING.
Registered as CHAMPION-AF; primary completion in the file is later than the publication of PMID 41910347, so the relationship needs checking. Registry status ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING.
Closure versus NOAC in AF with PCI. Registry status RECRUITING.

designs.primary: Reconstructed individual patient data meta-analysis from published Kaplan-Meier curves with flexible parametric and landmark models, one-stage random effects, pre-registered on PROSPERO, with a pre-specified update when NCT03642509 and NCT04226547 report
designs.alternative: Full IPD pooling through a trialist consortium, which would permit effect modification by CHA2DS2-VASc, HAS-BLED, device type and prior ICH

data_required: Published Kaplan-Meier curves and numbers at risk for all randomised closure trials; trial protocols for outcome definitions
data_sources: Published trial reports in the store
feasibility: High for reconstructed IPD with the owner's existing workflow; moderate for full IPD, which depends on sponsor and trialist agreement.
overlap: No overlap with active owner projects; fits the same-day SRMA workflow when the next trial reports.

G1.note: Stroke, bleeding and death on a very common decision in atrial fibrillation.

G2.note: Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved); equipoise judged on trial evidence only. Trials in the subset conflict on non-inferiority (PMIDs 41910347, 41849741).

G3.note: No meta-analysis in a target- or general-tier journal appears in the appraised subset in the past 24 months for this comparison, but the subset is incomplete and this must be checked in the adversarial search; of the registered trials only NCT03642509 (750) falls due within 24 months and is not alone adequately powered.

G4.note: A guideline committee would cite a time-varying analysis; aggregate risk ratios hide the early-harm and late-benefit pattern.

G5.note: Differs from the three October 2026 aggregate meta-analyses by analysing the time axis and event types, but is close to a repeat synthesis of the same trials and the adversarial check must test this.

impact.why: Atrial fibrillation anticoagulation decisions affect a very large population with hard outcomes.

novelty.why: Aggregate meta-analyses exist; the time-varying angle is the new element.

equipoise.why: Trials in the subset disagree on non-inferiority.

design.why: Reconstructed IPD is credible but limited by curve quality and outcome definitions.

timeliness.why: Several trials in the store are due to report between 2026 and 2029.

citation.why: Closure trials appear in the NEJM and Circulation, but meta-analyses of aggregate data carry less weight.

feasibility.why: Matches the owner's reconstructed IPD workflow.

next_actions: Search PubMed and PROSPERO for any existing IPD or reconstructed-IPD analysis of closure trials
Extract Kaplan-Meier curves and numbers at risk from the trials in the store
Register the protocol with a pre-specified update trigger

title: Prospective pre-registered synthesis of catheter-directed and mechanical therapies in intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism on hard clinical outcomes

pico.population: Adults with intermediate-risk or intermediate-high-risk acute pulmonary embolism
pico.intervention: Catheter-directed thrombolysis, ultrasound-facilitated thrombolysis or large-bore mechanical thrombectomy plus anticoagulation
pico.outcomes: All-cause death, haemodynamic decompensation, major bleeding, and the original hierarchical composites reported on a common scale
pico.timing: In hospital to 30 days, and longest available follow-up

decision: Which patients with intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism should receive an interventional therapy, and which modality.
decision_maker: Pulmonary embolism response teams, interventional cardiologists, pulmonologists and radiologists; guideline committees
why_now: Four randomised trials in the subset reported between 2025 and 2026 with different comparators and composites: PEERLESS (PMID 39470698), STORM-PE (PMID 41183181), a trial of ultrasound-facilitated fibrinolysis (PMID 41910345) and a trial of catheter-directed thrombolysis (PMID 42678032). A registry shows a shift from catheter-directed thrombolysis to thrombectomy (PMID 41739022). Further trials are registered, including NCT05591118, NCT06055920 and NCT04430569.

competing.note: PE-TRACT; catheter-directed therapy trial. Registry status ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING.
The PEERLESS II Study; comparator not stated in the trials file. Registry status ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING.
PEITHO-3. Registry status ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING.
STRATIFY-II; embolectomy, low-dose thrombolysis or heparin. Registry status RECRUITING.
ULTRA-PE. Registry status RECRUITING.

designs.primary: Pre-registered living network meta-analysis with a Bayesian random-effects model and a common hierarchical outcome definition, updated as each registered trial reports
designs.alternative: Reconstructed IPD of win-ratio components where full IPD are unavailable

data_required: Published results of all randomised trials with hard outcome components; registered protocols
data_sources: Published trial reports in the store
feasibility: High; network meta-analysis is within the owner's methods.
overlap: No overlap with active owner projects.

G1.note: Death and decompensation in a high-mortality acute setting.

G2.note: Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved); equipoise judged on trial evidence only. Trials in the subset use different composites, none shows a mortality difference, and several are small.

G3.note: Individual trials are each likely underpowered for death, so a pooled estimate is not expected from a single registered trial; PE-TRACT (500) and PEERLESS II (1200) will add data within 24 months. Adequate power of each cannot be judged from the file, so this gate needs the adversarial check.

G4.note: A pre-registered living network synthesis would be cited by guideline committees reconsidering advanced therapies.

G5.note: Not a repeat of an existing meta-analysis in the subset; the risk is a competing synthesis already in preparation.

impact.why: Pulmonary embolism is common and advanced therapy use is rising (PMID 41739022).

novelty.why: Pooled analyses of this field are likely to be in preparation elsewhere.

equipoise.why: Trials report composites and early surrogates without a mortality difference.

design.why: Heterogeneous comparators and outcomes limit network transitivity.

timeliness.why: Multiple trials are due to report within two years.

citation.why: Network meta-analyses in a hot field attract citations but not at the level of the trials.

next_actions: Search for existing pulmonary embolism intervention network meta-analyses
Draft a common outcome map across the four reported trials
Register the protocol with a trial-by-trial update plan

title: Value-of-information analysis for a hard-endpoint trial of renal denervation in hypertension

pico.population: Adults with uncontrolled or resistant hypertension
pico.intervention: Catheter-based renal denervation plus usual care
pico.outcomes: Modelled stroke, myocardial infarction, heart failure, death, and quality-adjusted life years with costs

decision: Whether funders should commission a hard-endpoint renal denervation trial, and its size.
decision_maker: Trial funders, health technology assessment bodies, guideline committees
why_now: Sham-controlled trials in the subset show blood pressure reductions (PMIDs 34010611, 36853250, 36130612) and a meta-analysis of ten sham-controlled trials (2478 patients) reports 24-hour systolic reductions of 4.4 mm Hg (95% CI 2.7 to 6.1) with an all-cause death odds ratio of 1.76 (95% CI 0.34 to 9.20) (PMID 39355923). A consensus statement positions the procedure as an adjunct (PMID 36790101). No trial in the subset reports clinical events.

competing.note: SPYRAL AFFIRM; global study of renal denervation. Registry status ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING.
EMBRACE; renal denervation, full title truncated in the file. Registry status NOT_YET_RECRUITING.
THRIVE; intravascular ultrasound renal denervation. Registry status RECRUITING.

designs.primary: Patient-level Markov microsimulation with probabilistic sensitivity analysis and expected value of perfect and partial perfect information, followed by sizing of a registry-based randomised trial
designs.alternative: Target trial emulation of blood pressure reduction effects on events in UK Biobank as a model input, with explicit limits

data_required: Blood pressure effects from sham trials, event risk equations, device and procedure costs, utility values
data_sources: Published sham-controlled trials in the store
feasibility: High; matches the owner's Markov microsimulation and value-of-information methods.
overlap: Method overlaps with the Impella microsimulation project but the topic does not.
target_journal: JAMA Cardiology or European Heart Journal

G1.note: Hypertension is among the commonest conditions and the decision is on events modelled from blood pressure.

G2.note: Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved); equipoise judged on trial evidence only. No hard-endpoint trial result exists in the subset.

G3.note: No trial in the file lists a hard-endpoint primary outcome within 24 months, though the primary outcome field is empty for most registry entries and must be checked.

G4.note: A value-of-information analysis justifies and sizes a trial, which funders would cite.

G5.note: The model rests on a blood pressure surrogate and may be judged surrogate-only by a target-journal editor; it passes only if framed as sizing a trial rather than estimating benefit.

impact.why: Very large population, though effect on events is modelled.

novelty.why: Cost-effectiveness models of renal denervation exist in the wider literature, which this subset does not show.

equipoise.why: Blood pressure effect is established; event effect is unknown.

timeliness.why: Device approvals and guideline interest are rising.

citation.why: Modelling papers on devices rarely reach the top citation decile.

feasibility.why: Direct fit with the owner's methods.

next_actions: Search for published renal denervation cost-effectiveness and value-of-information models
Extract treatment effects from sham-controlled trials in the store
Specify model structure and risk equations

status_history.reason: Proposed from the D9 landscape; G5 fails as currently framed.

title: Prospective synthesis of surgical left atrial appendage occlusion trials by atrial fibrillation status

pico.population: Adults undergoing cardiac surgery, with and without atrial fibrillation
pico.intervention: Concomitant surgical left atrial appendage occlusion
pico.outcomes: Stroke or systemic embolism, stroke, TIA or cardiovascular death, bleeding, death

decision: Whether to occlude the appendage at cardiac surgery in patients without a history of atrial fibrillation.
why_now: LAAOS III reduced stroke or systemic embolism in atrial fibrillation (hazard ratio 0.67; 95% CI 0.53 to 0.85; PMID 33999547), whereas OPINION in patients without atrial fibrillation did not reach significance (hazard ratio 0.83; 95% CI 0.61 to 1.14; PMID 40888584). LAACS-2, LAA-CLOSURE and LeAAPS are registered.

competing.note: LAACS-2. Registry status ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING.
LAA-CLOSURE. Registry status ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING.
LeAAPS. Registry status ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING.
LAAOS-4. Registry status RECRUITING.

designs.primary: Pre-registered meta-analysis with a pre-specified update at each readout and an interaction test by atrial fibrillation status
designs.alternative: Registry-based randomised trial in patients without atrial fibrillation

data_required: Trial-level results by atrial fibrillation status
feasibility: High for synthesis; trial option needs a surgical consortium.
overlap: No overlap with active owner projects.

G1.note: Stroke prevention at a common operation.

G2.note: Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved); equipoise judged on trial evidence only. Two randomised trials in the subset give different results by population.

G3.note: LAACS-2 (1500, primary completion 2025-10) and LAA-CLOSURE (1040, primary completion 2025-04) are past primary completion and are likely to report within 24 months; LeAAPS (6573) and LAAOS-4 (4000) follow later.

G4.note: A trial-level synthesis with an interaction test would be cited.

G5.note: With few trials the synthesis is a pooled analysis of a small number of studies until the registered trials report.

impact.why: Cardiac surgery volume is large but the incremental population is narrower.

novelty.why: Synthesis follows trials that will answer the question directly.

equipoise.why: The two trials point in the same direction with different significance.

design.why: Credible but dependent on pending readouts.

next_actions: Monitor readouts of the registered trials
Draft a protocol to register before the first readout
Re-test gates G3 and G5 after each readout

title: Heterogeneity of interatrial shunt effect by ejection fraction across the sham-controlled heart failure trials

pico.population: Adults with symptomatic heart failure with elevated filling pressures, by left ventricular ejection fraction
pico.outcomes: Hierarchical composite, heart failure events, safety events

decision: Whether shunt devices have any role in reduced or preserved ejection fraction heart failure.
decision_maker: Heart failure specialists and device regulators
why_now: REDUCE LAP-HF II showed no difference (win ratio 1.0; 95% CI 0.8 to 1.2; PMID 35120593) and RELIEVE-HF none overall (win ratio 0.86; 95% CI 0.61 to 1.22; PMID 39308371), with opposite signals by ejection fraction reported in RELIEVE-HF (PMID 39308371, PMID 42886087).

competing.note: RELIEVE-HFrEF. Registry status NOT_YET_RECRUITING.
PAST-HFrEF. Registry status RECRUITING.
Alleviant ALLAY-HFrEF. Registry status RECRUITING.
Alleviant ALLAY-HF. Registry status RECRUITING.

designs.primary: Pooled patient-level analysis of the sham-controlled trials with a pre-specified ejection fraction interaction
designs.alternative: Wait for the dedicated reduced-ejection-fraction trials

feasibility: Low; patient-level data are industry-held and win-ratio outcomes cannot be reconstructed from published curves.
overlap: No overlap with active owner projects.

G2.note: Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved); equipoise judged on trial evidence only. Trials show opposite subgroup signals.

G3.note: The reduced-ejection-fraction trials in the file have primary completion from 2028-12 onward, beyond 24 months, with small N (208 to 350).

G4.note: Without patient-level access no credible design exists, and published data do not permit the analysis.

G5.note: Relies on an unprespecified subgroup analysis of two trials, which is excluded by the gate.

impact.why: Device use is narrow after two neutral trials.

design.why: No credible design with available data.

next_actions: Re-assess when a reduced-ejection-fraction trial reports
Do not promote unless G4 and G5 change

status_history.reason: Recorded with failed gates G4 and G5; subspecialty only.
